examples.question_text:
By rounding each number to one significant figure, estimate:
(a) $43\times68$
(b) $624\div3.2$.
By rounding each number to one significant figure, estimate $6.4\times8.7$.
examples.solution_text:
Round each number to one significant figure.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}6.4\times8.7\\&\approx6\times9\\&=54\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: By rounding the number to one significant figure, estimate $76^2$.
By rounding each number to one significant figure, estimate $387\div7.6$.

examples.derivation: 43 rounds to 40 and 68 to 70; 40 × 70 = 2800. 624 rounds to 600 and 3.2 to 3; 600 ÷ 3 = 200. Both follow different-value adaptations of booklet Question 12(a,d).
6.4 rounds to 6 and 8.7 to 9; 6 × 9 = 54. This follows the decimal-product estimation method in booklet Question 12(b).
76 rounds to 80 before squaring; 80² = 6400. This follows booklet Question 12(c), with different values.
387 rounds to 400 and 7.6 to 8; 400 ÷ 8 = 50. This follows booklet Question 12(d), with different values.
